Risks.riskTitle: Unformalized timeline extension may disrupt acceptance, deployment, and post-contract delivery continuity
Risks.riskDescription: The project is likely to encounter delivery disruption and governance escalation because planned PAT, regression, deployment, and hypercare activities extend materially beyond the contractual end date without documented formal extension approval.

riskChain.rootCause: Original contractual timeline did not fully accommodate downstream PAT, regression, deployment, and hypercare effort, and no formal amendment is evidenced despite the operational plan extending 7 weeks beyond contract end.
riskChain.trigger: Contract end date of 2026-09-11 reached without approved amendment
riskChain.primaryRisk: Unformalized timeline extension may disrupt acceptance, deployment, and post-contract delivery continuity
riskChain.downstreamRisk: Critical downstream phases may be delayed, paused, or re-baselined due to governance and contractual uncertainty.

Risks.businessImpact: Potential unplanned commercial negotiation and delayed milestone realization for post-contract activities.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: Contractual end date is 2026-09-11; operational plan runs through 2026-10-30; schedule health is marked UNDER REVIEW; remaining work is misaligned: about 9 weeks of activity vs 5 contract weeks remaining; no formal extension documentation is evidenced.
Risks.currentContextReasoning: This is the strongest evidence-based future risk because timeline extension is already structurally embedded in the delivery plan while formal approval is not documented. Historical intelligence shows the same PAT/regression scope recognition issue previously emerged and was not demonstrably resolved at root cause level.

historicalCorrelation.similarHistoricalPattern: Historical risk R01: regression testing and extended PAT added after initiation and not part of original SOW
historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: Late recognition of PAT/regression effort created prior schedule and contractual exposure; historical mitigation quality was weak and closure evidence was not documented; current project still shows the same timeline-governance mismatch.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: If not formalized immediately, PAT and release planning may proceed on assumed extension only, increasing contractual ambiguity and delivery disruption across regression, deployment, and hypercare.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: Historical risk explicitly identified unplanned regression/PAT scope; current timeline still shows PAT and regression beyond contractual end date; current extensionDetected = true with 7-week inferred extension; no formal extension documentation exists.
Risks.leadingIndicators: Formal extension/amendment approval status; updated integrated master schedule publication; steering committee decision logs; milestone/payment alignment for post-2026-09-11 activities; any pause or ambiguity in PAT/regression planning.
Risks.predictiveInsight: Treat this as an immediate governance action rather than a passive schedule observation.
Risks.mitigation: Execute formal contract/timeline amendment aligned to actual planned completion dates; reconcile milestone dates, acceptance windows, and payment terms with revised timeline; obtain written steering-level approval for post-September delivery assumptions; publish a single approved integrated timeline covering PAT, regression, deployment, and hypercare.
Risks.recommendations: Do not allow PAT and release planning to proceed on assumed extension only; link approval of extended timeline to confirmed resources, acceptance criteria, and milestone funding.

Risks.riskTitle: Unresolved client dependencies may block Sprint 5 completion and reduce PAT readiness
Risks.riskDescription: The project is likely to face near-term execution slippage because unresolved client-side decisions and environment dependencies may prevent completion of release-critical work before PAT and integrated workflow validation.

riskChain.rootCause: Critical client inputs and environment-related decisions expected earlier in the lifecycle remain unresolved in Week 11, including chat escalation requirements, Azure monitoring confirmation, automation environment provisioning, and Guru Card assessment.
riskChain.trigger: High-severity dependencies remain open into Sprint 5
riskChain.primaryRisk: Unresolved client dependencies may block Sprint 5 completion and reduce PAT readiness
riskChain.downstreamRisk: Sprint 5 deliverables and PAT start/readiness may slip or enter with partial functionality.

Risks.businessImpact: Additional rework and coordination effort may increase delivery overhead.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: Multiple high-severity dependencies remain unresolved; dependencies expected by Week 2 are still pending in Week 11; critical path includes dependency resolution before PAT and go-live; schedule pressure is HIGH and buffer availability is NONE.
Risks.currentContextReasoning: The delivery pattern shows dependency-driven delays already active. With only one sprint left before PAT and with schedule pressure already high, unresolved client dependencies have strong causal potential to materialize as immediate delivery blockage.

historicalCorrelation.similarHistoricalPattern: Historical risks R03 and R02: sprint slip due to broader scope and client cloud environment dependencies; delayed customer feedback threatened sprint validation
historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: Dependency-driven sprint slippage recurred historically; customer feedback and validation latency historically affected downstream implementation; current project still has unresolved high-severity client dependencies in Week 11.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: If the open client dependencies are not resolved before Sprint 5 completion, PAT entry and downstream release milestones will likely slip, with incomplete environments or partially defined workflows impacting readiness.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: Historical sprint slip tied to scope breadth and cloud dependencies; current project pattern explicitly identifies dependency-driven delivery delays; unresolved items include Azure monitoring and automation environment provisioning; SOW-required client inputs expected by Week 2 were still pending by Week 11.
Risks.leadingIndicators: Status of four high-severity dependencies; dependency age and owner accountability; Sprint 5 blocked stories; environment readiness confirmations; PAT entry checklist completion.
Risks.predictiveInsight: Raise unresolved dependencies to steering level immediately.
Risks.mitigation: Escalate all four high-severity dependencies with dated owner commitments; define non-negotiable dependency deadlines tied to Sprint 5 and PAT entry; separate critical-path dependencies from desirable enhancements; create contingency paths for environment/testing gaps where technically feasible.
Risks.recommendations: Use daily dependency burn-down until PAT entry criteria are met; do not rely on informal verbal alignment for escalation workflows or monitoring processes.

Risks.riskTitle: PAT may surface acceptance-blocking defects and enhancements that extend stabilization beyond planned windows
Risks.riskDescription: The upcoming PAT phase is likely to generate additional defects, usability issues, and enhancement debates that exceed the current stabilization capacity, reducing the probability of smooth acceptance and downstream release readiness.

riskChain.rootCause: The project shows an active feedback-driven development loop, significant backlog volume, UI/UX defect concentration, and incomplete closure of prior sprint early access review outputs, indicating residual quality and acceptance volatility entering PAT.
riskChain.trigger: PAT feedback continues to produce defects and enhancement requests
riskChain.primaryRisk: PAT may surface acceptance-blocking defects and enhancements that extend stabilization beyond planned windows
riskChain.downstreamRisk: PAT exit may be delayed and regression may expand due to unresolved acceptance defects.

Risks.businessImpact: Additional defect fixing and retesting may consume effort not planned in the original baseline.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: 53 total work items in backlog; UI-related bugs make up a significant proportion; PAT early feedback is generating defects and enhancement requests; Sprint 3 Early Access Review is still in progress as of 2026-08-13; quality health is UNDER REVIEW.
Risks.currentContextReasoning: Current evidence shows backlog accumulation, UI-related issues, and iterative PAT feedback already creating rework before formal PAT has started. Historical intelligence confirms this review-feedback pattern is recurrent and materially impacts validation-heavy phases.

historicalCorrelation.similarHistoricalPattern: Historical risks R02 and R01: customer feedback delay impacted validation and implementation; expanded PAT/regression effort created delivery exposure
historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: Feedback-cycle backlog accumulation is a strong historical pattern; customer validation timing historically affected downstream implementation; historical test/release scope expansion aligns with current acceptance risk.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: PAT is likely to generate more defects and enhancement requests than the current stabilization window can comfortably absorb, increasing the chance of delayed acceptance, expanded regression, and elevated hypercare load.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: Historical risk centered on delayed customer feedback affecting validation; current project uses repeated early access reviews after each sprint; PAT early verification generated defects and enhancement requests; Sprint 3 PAT early access review remained in progress during Sprint 4.
Risks.leadingIndicators: PAT defect inflow rate; open defect count by severity; enhancement vs defect classification trend; UI/UX issue closure rate; Sprint 3/4 review closure before PAT start.
Risks.predictiveInsight: Use phased acceptance if full defect clearance is unrealistic.
Risks.mitigation: Establish PAT entry and exit criteria with severity-based acceptance thresholds; triage defects separately from enhancements and defer non-critical enhancements; prioritize UI/UX issues that affect workflow completion or user trust; reserve explicit defect-resolution capacity during PAT and regression.
Risks.recommendations: Track PAT defect aging and reopen rates daily; require strict change control for enhancement requests raised during PAT.

Risks.riskTitle: Enhancement-driven scope expansion may erode final sprint focus and delay release-critical completion
Risks.riskDescription: The project may experience late-stage scope creep as enhancement requests and newly added technical work continue to compete with defect closure and release-critical deliverables, reducing control over what is required for acceptance.

riskChain.rootCause: PAT feedback includes enhancement requests, some issues are already classified as enhancements, and additional technical scope elements have appeared during execution, indicating baseline control is weakening during the most schedule-sensitive stage.
riskChain.trigger: Enhancement requests continue to be accepted into Sprint 5
riskChain.primaryRisk: Enhancement-driven scope expansion may erode final sprint focus and delay release-critical completion
riskChain.downstreamRisk: Release-critical work may be delayed by non-essential enhancement effort.

Risks.businessImpact: Unplanned effort may be absorbed without formal budget adjustment.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: Some issues are marked as enhancements; Sprint 5 includes enhancement feedback from Vivli team; new functionality and technical additions appeared during execution; scope drift assessed as MODERATE.
Risks.currentContextReasoning: This risk is supported by current evidence of enhancement-driven backlog growth and execution drift. Historical signals show broader scope and added test/release work have already affected delivery predictability in the same client context.

historicalCorrelation.similarHistoricalPattern: Historical risks R01 and R03: regression/PAT effort added after initiation; broader scope contributed to sprint slip
historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: Late recognition of additional test/release scope recurred historically; broader scope contributed to prior sprint slippage; current drift analysis shows multiple scope additions and enhancement expansion.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: If non-critical enhancements continue to enter the active delivery plan, final sprint capacity will be diluted, release-critical items may slip, and acceptance criteria may become harder to stabilize.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: Historical risk explicitly identified unplanned regression/PAT scope; broader scope and client dependencies caused earlier sprint slip; current drift analysis identifies enhancement-driven scope expansion and added technical components.
Risks.leadingIndicators: Count of enhancement requests added after Sprint 4; defect-to-enhancement ratio in active backlog; number of newly introduced user stories or technical tasks; weekly variance against release-critical scope; formal change approvals recorded.
Risks.predictiveInsight: Use steering-approved scope guardrails for remaining delivery.
Risks.mitigation: Implement immediate change control distinguishing defects, mandatory compliance gaps, and optional enhancements; freeze non-critical enhancements before PAT unless approved by governance forum; re-baseline Sprint 5 against release-critical outcomes only; maintain a deferred enhancement backlog for post-deployment or phase 2 consideration.
Risks.recommendations: Require business value and timeline impact statement for every new enhancement request; report enhancement intake separately from defect closure in weekly governance.

Risks.riskTitle: Late-stage GPT-5 Mini migration may destabilize final validation and release readiness
Risks.riskDescription: Migrating services to GPT-5 Mini in the final sprint may introduce functional, integration, or performance issues that reduce confidence in PAT outcomes and consume limited stabilization capacity before release.

riskChain.rootCause: A significant technical change is scheduled late in the delivery lifecycle while quality health is under review, backlog remains elevated, and there is limited schedule buffer for revalidation if the migration causes regressions.
riskChain.trigger: GPT-5 Mini migration proceeds in Sprint 5
riskChain.primaryRisk: Late-stage GPT-5 Mini migration may destabilize final validation and release readiness
riskChain.downstreamRisk: Additional validation and rework may delay PAT readiness or PAT exit.

Risks.businessImpact: Extra engineering and testing effort may be required to stabilize model behavior.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: Sprint 5 includes migration to GPT-5 Mini; LLM evaluation is still ongoing in Sprint 4; quality health is UNDER REVIEW; schedule buffer is effectively none.
Risks.currentContextReasoning: This is a relevant but secondary risk: it is directly evidenced in current sprint plans and becomes more material because it occurs in the final sprint under high schedule pressure and constrained quality buffer.

historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: No direct historical analogue in provided historical risks; enriched by current pattern of late-stage complexity and execution drift.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: If the GPT-5 Mini migration introduces functional or integration regressions, PAT and regression phases will absorb additional validation and rework effort, increasing the probability of acceptance delay and elevated hypercare load.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: Current technical architecture evolution pattern indicates late-stage technical refinement risk; historical context indirectly supports increased exposure when broadening work is introduced under schedule pressure.
Risks.leadingIndicators: Migration completion status; post-migration defect count; output accuracy/quality metrics; rollback readiness; integration test pass rate after migration.
Risks.predictiveInsight: Avoid coupling migration with non-essential enhancements in the same sprint.
Risks.mitigation: Perform impact assessment before migration cutover; define and test rollback plan; run targeted regression on both use cases immediately after migration; protect PAT entry with explicit migration completion criteria.
Risks.recommendations: Obtain business sign-off on acceptable model behavior thresholds; escalate immediately if migration reduces output quality or integration stability.

Risks.riskTitle: Resource continuity beyond contract end may be insufficient for release and hypercare execution
Risks.riskDescription: If vendor and client resource commitments are not explicitly secured beyond the contractual end date, the project may face continuity gaps during regression, deployment, training, and hypercare when experienced resources are most needed.

riskChain.rootCause: The delivery plan extends through 2026-10-30 but documented contractual commitment ends on 2026-09-11, and no confirmed resource extension is evidenced for the post-contract execution period.
riskChain.trigger: No written resource commitment is issued for post-2026-09-11 period
riskChain.primaryRisk: Resource continuity beyond contract end may be insufficient for release and hypercare execution
riskChain.downstreamRisk: Regression, deployment, or hypercare tasks may slip due to staffing discontinuity.

Risks.businessImpact: Emergency backfill or unplanned extension negotiation may increase cost.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: Activities are planned through 2026-10-30; contract term ends 2026-09-11; no documented resource plan for post-contract period; resource feasibility rated as moderate risk.
Risks.currentContextReasoning: This risk follows directly from the evidenced mismatch between contract term and operational timeline. It is especially relevant because release and hypercare phases depend on continuity, specialized knowledge, and timely support response.

historicalCorrelation.similarHistoricalPattern: Historical risk R01 supports recurrence of downstream unplanned effort beyond original assumptions
historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: Historical governance/timeline mismatch created unresolved downstream exposure; weak formalization of extended effort historically increased recurrence risk.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: Without explicit post-contract resource commitments, final execution phases may face continuity gaps, slower issue resolution, and reduced deployment/hypercare stability.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: Historical governance/timeline mismatch created downstream unplanned effort; current operational timeline extends well beyond the contractual term with no formal resource continuity evidence.
Risks.leadingIndicators: Resource extension approvals; named staffing plan for post-contract phases; attrition or reassignment notices; client UAT/training attendance commitments; coverage plan for deployment and hypercare.
Risks.predictiveInsight: Include resource continuity as a formal condition in extension approval.
Risks.mitigation: Secure written resource commitments through planned hypercare end date; confirm named backup resources for critical technical and operational roles; align resource plan with amended timeline and milestone approvals; validate client-side availability for PAT, training, deployment, and support windows.
Risks.recommendations: Track key-person dependency exposure for final phases; do not assume existing team availability through October without documented confirmation.
